items.title: Blom rank-normal scores for pooled draws
items.statement: Pool scalar draws, assign average ranks to ties, and map each rank r to Phi^{-1}((r-3/8)/(S+1/4)).
items.strategy: Define the finite rank-score transform and state the normal-CDF inverse interface.

items.title: Left empirical quantile of finite draws
items.statement: For sorted finite draws x_(1)<=...<=x_(S), set Q_S(u)=x_(ceil(Su)) for 0<u<=1, retaining ties.
items.strategy: Specify the inverse-ECDF convention and tie handling.

items.title: Standard Cauchy probability law
items.statement: Define the standard Cauchy law as the probability measure with density 1/(pi*(1+x^2)) relative to Lebesgue measure; prove the normalization and well-definedness.
items.strategy: Construct the density measure, evaluate its mass on symmetric compact intervals, and use monotone convergence.

items.title: Functional-specific effective sample size
items.statement: For a stationary scalar functional with absolutely summable autocorrelations and positive tau=1+2 sum_{k>=1} rho(k), define ESS_h(n)=n/tau, conditionally on the corresponding asymptotic-variance regime.
items.strategy: Define the variance-equivalent sample size for a chosen functional without asserting a CLT.

items.title: Split R-hat from multiple chains
items.statement: Split equal-length finite chains into first and last halves, compute W, B and V+, and return sqrt(V+/W) when W>0.
items.strategy: Give the finite split, within/between variance and nonestimable W=0 branch.

items.title: Split multi-chain autocorrelation effective sample size
items.statement: Split equal-length finite chains (discarding a middle draw when odd), combine split-chain within/between autocorrelations with Geyer positive/monotone paired truncation and antithetic odd/even averaging, and return the retained split sample size divided by tau subject to the documented finite software cap.
items.strategy: Define the split, between/within adjustment, biased autocovariances, paired truncation, antithetic averaging, cap and nonestimable branches.

items.title: Rank-normalized folded split R-hat
items.statement: Return the maximum of split R-hat on pooled Blom normal scores and on Blom scores of absolute deviations from the pooled median.
items.strategy: Compose pooled rank normalization, splitting, folding, and the two split statistics.

items.title: Bulk effective sample size
items.statement:
**Inputs:** $M\ge2$ equal-length scalar chains with $N\ge2$ observations each. Pool all draws and apply
[[def-blom-rank-normalization-for-pooled-draws]]. Apply
[[alg-multichain-effective-sample-size]] to the resulting $M$ transformed
chains. The output is the **bulk effective sample size** for this procedure.

Rank normalization makes this diagnostic finite for every finite real-valued
draw array, including arrays whose target distribution might have infinite mean
or variance. It is an efficiency diagnostic for the transformed values and is
not, by itself, a Monte Carlo standard error for the original posterior mean.
items.strategy: Define bulk ESS as the ESS procedure applied to rank-normalized draws.

items.title: Tail effective sample size
items.statement:
**Inputs:** $M\ge2$ equal-length chains of scalar draws with $N\ge2$ observations each. Pool the draws and
calculate $q_{.05}=Q_S(.05)$ and $q_{.95}=Q_S(.95)$ using
[[def-empirical-left-quantile-for-finite-draws]]. For each
$p\in\{.05,.95\}$, form the bounded indicator chains
$I^{(p)}_{m,n}=\mathbf1\{x_{m,n}\le q_p\}$, pool their values, apply
[[def-blom-rank-normalization-for-pooled-draws]], and apply
[[alg-multichain-effective-sample-size]] to the transformed indicator chains.

If either indicator ESS is not estimable, return **not estimable**. Otherwise
return the minimum of the two values. This is a tail-focused efficiency
diagnostic; it does not establish that a quantile estimate has a specified
error bound.
items.strategy: Localize ESS to the two tail quantile indicators and report the minimum.

items.title: Quantile Monte Carlo standard error
items.statement:
**Inputs:** $M\ge2$ equal-length scalar chains with $N\ge2$ observations each, a quantile level $\alpha\in(0,1)$,
and the fixed levels $u_-=.16$ and $u_+=.84$ used for a one-standard-error
approximation.

1. Pool the draws and compute $\widehat q_\alpha=Q_S(\alpha)$ by
   [[def-empirical-left-quantile-for-finite-draws]]. Form the indicator chains
   $I_{m,n}=\mathbf1\{x_{m,n}\le\widehat q_\alpha\}$, Blom-normalize their
   pooled values by [[def-blom-rank-normalization-for-pooled-draws]], and
   compute $E_\alpha$ with [[alg-multichain-effective-sample-size]]. If the
   indicator chains are constant or $E_\alpha$ is not estimable, return
   **not estimable**.
2. Set $a=E_\alpha\alpha+1$ and
   $b=E_\alpha(1-\alpha)+1$. For $u\in(0,1)$, define the lower Beta quantile
   $Q_{a,b}(u)=\inf\{t\in[0,1]:F_{a,b}(t)\ge u\}$, where
   $F_{a,b}(t)=\operatorname{Beta}(a,b)((0,t])$ and
   [[def-beta-distribution]] supplies the probability measure. Let
   $v_-=Q_{a,b}(u_-)$ and $v_+=Q_{a,b}(u_+)$.
3. Return the approximate Monte Carlo error interval
   $[Q_S(v_-),Q_S(v_+)]$ and the estimate
   $$\widehat{\operatorname{MCSE}}(\widehat q_\alpha)=\frac{Q_S(v_+)-Q_S(v_-)}2.$$

All Beta shape parameters are positive because $E_\alpha>0$ and
$0<\alpha<1$. This is a finite-run approximation, not a theorem that the
interval has a prescribed coverage probability. Its statistical interpretation
requires conditions for the relevant quantile and indicator-chain limit
behavior; none are asserted here.
items.strategy: Define the Beta-quantile approximation and its finite, nonestimable boundaries.

title: MCMC diagnostics and finite-run limitations — Examples

items.title: Thinning lowers observed lag correlation but discards information
items.statement: For a stationary two-state chain with lag correlation 0.8^k, thinning by ten lowers retained lag-one correlation but lowers total ESS under a fixed transition budget.
items.strategy: Verify the transition law, correlation powers, geometric long-run variance and retained-sample ESS.

items.title: A shared missed region in a finite funnel-shaped target
items.statement:
This finite funnel-shaped model has state space $E=\{n\}\cup B$ with the
discrete sigma-algebra, where $n=(0,0)$ is the narrow state and
$B=\{(v,x):v\in\{1,2,3,4\},\ x\in\{-2,-1,1,2\}\}$ is the broad region.
Let $\pi(n)=1/2$ and give each state in $B$ mass $1/32$. Let $K$ fix $n$ and
cycle through the 16 states of $B$ in lexicographic order, beginning at
$(1,-2)$. Let $\Pi$ be the independent-refresh kernel
$\Pi(x,\{y\})=\pi(y)$ and put $P=.99K+.01\Pi$. Start four chains at $(1,-2)$
and use independent transition randomness. On an event of probability
$.99^{124}$, all 124 transitions use $K$. Every chain then misses the narrow
state, even though it has target mass $1/2$. On that event the rank-normalized
folded split $\widehat R$ for each coordinate is $\sqrt{15/16}<1$.
items.strategy: Verify the finite invariant target, positive-probability missed-region event, and identical split-chain variance ratios.

items.title: Heavy tails and a location shift in split R-hat
items.statement: The standard Cauchy has no finite second moment, while an explicit finite location-shift array has raw and rank-normalized split R-hat sqrt(7/4) and folded R-hat sqrt(3/4).
items.strategy: Prove the Cauchy second-moment divergence and compute the raw, rank-normalized and folded finite variance ratios.

items.title: Centered eight-schools runs show small R-hat with low tail ESS
items.statement: Report Vehtari et al.'s centered eight-schools simulation outputs, including a near-one R-hat with low tail ESS and a thinned run whose diagnostics failed to reveal the observed problem; classify these as empirical results.
items.strategy: Transcribe the source-reported simulation results and state their empirical, non-theorem status.
